newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs target 132.38 but correction looms.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs target 132.38 but correction looms.

text.p: The September BTP contract on LIFFE may hit its all time high at 132.38 on Monday, but longer term, the market is due a fairly sharp correction, technical analysts said.

"I think this one is in need of a correction at some stage," said Marc Ostwald, technical analyst at London Bond Broking. "It looks totally overstreched to me -- three points in four days is at best tenuous."
September BTPs rose from a low of 129.07 on June 10 to a high of 132.09 on June 13. By 0749 GMT on Monday they were up 49 basis points at 132.28, off an earlier contract high of 132.35.
Ostwald put support at Friday's low of 131.10, ahead of congestion at 130.75,85.
"But if we see a proper retracement, we would probably go back to the gap at 130.07,08," he said. Charts show the market hit a daily high of 130.07 on June 10, then a low of 130.08 the following day.
Analysts at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said daily indicators for BTPs showed divergences, adding doubt to the endurance of the upmove.
"It seems unlikely for gains to extend to the 132.79 wave extension in the short term," they said in a note.
DMG said support near 131.08 was key for the next trend. "A break would trigger a retest of the uptrend in the area of 129.80, and likely deeper to the uptrend near 129.30," they said.
If that support goes, deeper declines over the following weeks were expected to the 50 percent retracement area near 127.85, they said.
By 0805 GMT, the September Eurolira contract was up one basis point at 93.41.
